title: Prevent metering leakage from API key template clones across subaccounts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Several customers operating subaccounts reported unexpected cross-project usage appearing on unrelated projects after teams used our API key template cloning feature. This ticket tracks the investigation and remediation to ensure API key template clones receive correct ownership and do not cause metering or rate-limit attribution leakage.
reproduction_steps: Create a tenant with a project A and a project B
Create an API key template bound to project A that includes a preconfigured integration metadata field (template_id)
Use the template cloning flow to create a new key for a subaccount derived from project B (UI or API path /keys/clone)
Make requests with the cloned key and observe the usage counters in /billing/usage and the rate-limiter dashboard
Confirm that counters increment against project A or template owner rather than project B
investigation_summary: Initial triage shows cloned keys inherit a template attribution token and sometimes reuse an internal binding record (claim_id) stored in the key metadata. When propagation happens quickly after clone, the claim cache in ingress service still maps the token to the original project. Logs (proxy-ingress) show the key_id was new, but attribution lookup prioritized template_claim_id over explicit project binding, causing counts to attribute to the template owner. Grafana panels show a correlated spike in template-owner project usage when large numbers of clones were created in short windows.
root_cause: Cloning flow copies template attribution metadata (template_claim_id) into the key document without regenerating or re-binding a new claim mapping for the destination project. The attribution resolution code path prioritized an existing claim_id present on key metadata before checking runtime project bindings and cache TTLs, leading to misattribution when cache was warm for the template owner.
proposed_solution: On key clone: clear template-specific claim metadata and trigger an on-create binding generation that binds claim->project_id for the new key
Update attribution resolution to prioritize explicit project_id in key metadata and fall back to claim_id only when no explicit binding exists
Add a migration job to scan recent clones and re-run attribution for events in the last 30 days, producing a reclassification report
Harden rate-limiter counters to include key_id and project_id multi-dimensionally to avoid shared counters when attribution is ambiguous
Add unit + integration tests for clone path and attribution lookup cache behavior
acceptance_criteria: New clones no longer cause usage to appear in the template-owner project in staging and canary environments
Automation test covers clone -> immediate request pattern and verifies correct project attribution
Migration reattributes historical usage for identified affected keys and produces a reconciled billing delta report
Rate-limiter dashboards show counters tagged by both key_id and project_id for at least 14 days post-deploy
Post-deploy monitoring alert in place if >0.1% of clone-created-key requests are attributed to a different project over a 24h window
rollout_plan: Implement server-side fix behind feature flag attr-fix/ENG-27834
Deploy to staging and run automated clone-attribution tests
Canary deploy to a small subset of production (5% traffic) with monitoring gates
Run migration job during low-traffic window; verify reattribute report against accounting ledger
Gradually increase canary to 100% and then remove feature flag
Notify billing ops and affected customers with the reconciliation report
